title: Overview & Executive Summary
items: MODEL MIND
Decision TreeVisualization
Product specification, UI/UX blueprint, feature inventory, visualization plan, and step-by-step implementation guide

PROJECT GOALBuild an interactive, accurate, educational decision-tree explorer where users can train a model, inspect every node and branch, trace predictions, explore 2D/3D decision regions, and understand model quality. All displayed model values must be derived from the trained model and selected dataset.
Prepared for: Model Mind
Document type: Editable implementation report (.docx)
Version: 1.0  |  11 October 2026

title: How to use this report
items: Treat this document as the product requirements document (PRD) and build checklist. Implement Phase 1 before moving to advanced 3D and model-comparison features. The counts below are recommended scope counts—not a requirement to place every control on one crowded screen.
Use the feature inventory to define routes, tabs, panels, and acceptance criteria.
Use the implementation phases in order. Complete and test each phase before proceeding.
Use the API/data-contract section to keep the frontend and model backend consistent.
Use the final checklist before calling the visualization ready for real users.

title: 1. Executive summary
items: Decision Tree Visualization should function as both a model-analysis workspace and a learning tool. A user should be able to load a dataset, select a target column, configure and train a decision tree, inspect the complete tree, select any node, see its statistics, test a row, trace its root-to-leaf path, and compare model quality. For classification, the interface should explain class distributions and classification metrics. For regression, it should explain predicted numeric values and regression metrics.
Planning item
Recommendation
Primary user goal
Understand how a trained decision tree makes a prediction and how reliable it is.
Recommended main navigation
8 top-level sections; details listed in Section 3.
Recommended visualizations
10 core visualization types; 4 advanced/optional types.
Main tree interaction
Select a node to synchronize node details, branch highlighting, rule text, and prediction path.
MVP delivery
Dataset upload, training, full 2D tree, node details, prediction path, core metrics, feature importance, 2D boundary.
Advanced delivery
3D exploration, pruning comparison, local explanations, exports, model comparison, accessibility refinements.
Visual direction
Warm white/charcoal neutral surfaces with emerald, muted purple, amber, and coral accents; avoid blue as the main brand color.

NON-NEGOTIABLE ACCURACY RULEDo not hardcode example thresholds, node counts, impurity values, class probabilities, accuracy, or feature importance. Derive them from the actual trained model, the actual evaluation split, and the currently selected dataset.

title: 2. Product goals and user journeys
items: 2.1 Main goals
Teach the structure of a decision tree: root, internal nodes, branches, and leaves.
Make the model explainable: show the conditions applied at each node and the final root-to-leaf rule.
Support practical analysis: train, evaluate, compare, and export the tree.
Connect views: selecting a node or prediction path should update related details where possible.
Support both classification and regression trees without mixing incompatible metrics.
Remain usable for small trees and deep trees with hundreds or thousands of nodes.
2.2 Main user journey
Open Decision Tree from the Model Mind sidebar.
Upload a CSV or choose a sample dataset.
Review detected columns, missing values, data types, and target-column options.
Select the target column and choose classification or regression.
Configure split criterion, maximum depth, minimum samples, pruning, and test split.
Train the model and inspect evaluation metrics.
Open Tree Visualization and select any node to inspect its details.
Open Prediction Explorer, choose a row or enter feature values, and follow the path to a leaf.
Explore the 2D boundary, optional 3D view, feature importance, and rules.
Export the tree, rules, metrics, or a prediction explanation.

title: 5. Dataset intake and preprocessing features
items: The dataset flow should be explicit and safe. Do not silently choose a target column or silently discard rows without telling the user.
Feature
Expected behavior
Validation / edge cases
Upload CSV
Support drag-and-drop and file picker; show filename and row/column count.
Reject unsupported format, empty file, corrupted file, and excessively large uploads with clear messages.
Preview table
Show first 10–25 rows, column names, inferred types, and scrollable data.
Escape displayed text; do not execute cell contents.
Target selection
Require the user to choose the column to predict.
Target cannot be missing or identical to a feature after preprocessing.
Task type
Suggest classification for categorical targets and regression for numeric targets, but allow user confirmation.
Warn about ambiguous numeric class labels.
Feature selection
Allow selecting usable predictors and excluding ID/leakage columns.
Keep selected features consistent between training and prediction input.
Missing values
Report missing counts and percentages by column.
Use an explicit strategy: reject, drop, or impute; display what was done.
Categorical features
Encode categories consistently, ideally with a fitted preprocessing pipeline.
Unknown categories at prediction time need a defined fallback/error.
Train/test split
Expose test size and random seed; use stratification for classification when appropriate.
Guard against tiny classes or too few rows.
Data leakage warning
Flag obvious ID columns and suspicious target-like predictors where possible.
Treat warnings as advisory, not definitive proof.
Dataset summary
Show row count, feature count, target distribution, data types, missingness.
Separate preprocessed feature count from original column count.

Classification: gini; regression: squared_error.
Only show criteria supported by the selected estimator/version.

Default None or a conservative configurable value; explain overfitting trade-off.
Allow None and positive integers; prevent invalid input.

Default 2.
Integer >= 2 or supported fraction.

Default 1.
Integer >= 1 or supported fraction.

Default None.
Optional complexity constraint.

best by default; random optional where supported.
Explain deterministic vs randomized split search.

None by default; optional balanced setting for classification.
Do not show for regression.
Train/test ratio
Default 80/20.
Show exact row counts after split.

Default fixed seed for reproducibility; editable.
Persist it with run metadata.

title: 7. Full tree visualization: specification
items: This is the core of the product. The tree must reflect the exact trained estimator and its preprocessing pipeline.
7.1 What every node should show
Node type
Required display
Optional display
Root / internal split
Node ID; split condition such as feature ≤ threshold; sample count; impurity; class distribution or regression value.
Weighted samples; split gain; proportion of dataset; depth.
Leaf / terminal node
Node ID; predicted class or numeric output; sample count; class distribution for classification.
Purity; prediction probability; rule path; support/coverage.
Selected node
Strong outline; selected node ID; ancestor path; outgoing branches highlighted.
Pinned node details and linked row samples.
Branch / edge
True/left and False/right semantics consistent with the model; directional connector.
Sample counts on each branch and edge hover details.
7.2 Required tree canvas interactions (10)
Select a node by click/tap; selection persists until another node is selected.
Zoom in and zoom out using buttons and trackpad/mouse gestures where supported.
Fit entire tree to available canvas.
Pan the canvas without accidentally selecting a node.
Expand/collapse a subtree for readability; collapsed nodes must indicate hidden descendants.
Switch layout: top-to-bottom and left-to-right.
Toggle node labels: compact, standard, and detailed.
Reset layout and zoom.
Highlight a prediction path from root to selected leaf.
Export current tree view to a usable image/vector format.
7.3 Layout and scale
Use a hierarchical tree layout; connectors must not overlap node text.
Small trees should fit automatically. Large trees should support collapse, search, minimap or viewport navigation, and progressive rendering.
Never shrink text to unreadable sizes just to fit the whole tree.
Provide a synchronized accessible outline/tree list for keyboard navigation.
Use color as a secondary cue; labels, shapes, and branch text must still communicate meaning.

title: 8. Node details panel: recommended 12 fields
items: Field
Meaning / source
Node ID
Stable node index from the fitted tree.
Node type
Root, internal split, or leaf.
Depth
Number of edges from root.
Split feature
Feature used at this split; not applicable to a leaf.
Threshold / condition
Actual threshold and comparator from the estimator.
Impurity / criterion value
Gini or entropy for classification; criterion-specific value for regression.
Samples
Training samples reaching the node; label whether weighted or unweighted.
Weighted samples
Show when available and distinguish from raw count.
Class distribution / target summary
Per-class counts for classification; value summary for regression.
Predicted output
Predicted class or numeric value at this node.
Child nodes
Left/right child IDs and branch conditions; none for a leaf.
Node coverage
Percentage of training rows reaching this node, clearly labeled as training coverage.

IMPORTANT SEMANTICSFor scikit-learn trees, a common split convention is left child for feature value ≤ threshold and right child for feature value > threshold. Confirm and implement the estimator's actual semantics; never infer branch labels from visual position alone.

title: 9. Visualization catalogue: 10 core types + 4 advanced
items: Visualization
Purpose
Priority / implementation notes
Full decision tree
Explain complete model structure and individual splits.
Core; hierarchical SVG/canvas renderer.
Prediction path overlay
Show the exact route for one sample from root to leaf.
Core; synchronize with selected row and node.
2D decision boundary
Show how two selected features separate predictions.
Core; sample grid and actual model predictions; explain other features are held at a defined value or strategy.
Feature importance bar chart
Rank global importance of features.
Core; label method, e.g. impurity-based importance.
Class/target distribution
Show target balance or regression target distribution.
Core; bar chart for classes, histogram for numeric targets.
Confusion matrix
Compare actual vs predicted classes.
Core for classification only; labels and counts required.
Classification report
Compare precision, recall, F1, support per class.
Core for classification; macro/weighted averages explained.
Regression actual-vs-predicted scatter
See prediction fit and systematic errors.
Core for regression only.
Regression residual plot
Inspect residual patterns and outliers.
Core for regression only.
Tree complexity / pruning comparison
Compare depth, leaves, and validation score across pruning settings.
MVP can show current depth/leaves; full path is advanced.
3D feature-space exploration
Explore three selected features and sample clusters/regions.
Advanced; use WebGL-capable chart library; avoid false claims about a continuous surface.
Permutation importance
Estimate score drop after shuffling a feature.
Advanced; computationally more expensive; use held-out data.
Partial dependence / ICE
Explore average or individual response changes for selected features.
Advanced; explain assumptions and feature interactions.
ROC / precision-recall curve
Evaluate binary or supported multiclass scores.
Advanced; only when valid probability/score outputs and task setup support it.
9.1 2D decision boundary requirements
X-axis and Y-axis feature selectors.
Actual data points, colored by true class or target; provide a legend.
Background decision regions predicted by the trained model.
Tooltip with row identifier (if available), feature values, true target, predicted target, and confidence/probabilities where meaningful.
A visible explanation of how non-plotted features are fixed or handled; otherwise the displayed 2D projection can be misleading.
Option to show misclassified points on the held-out set.
Reset zoom and download chart.
9.2 3D visualization requirements
Three independent feature selectors for X, Y, and Z; prevent selecting the same feature for all axes unless explicitly allowed.
Rotate, zoom, reset camera, and inspect a point by click/tap.
Legend and consistent class colors shared with other views.
Show decision regions only when they are computed from the actual estimator and clearly explain the sampling/resolution used.
Allow users to switch to a 2D slice or pairwise view when the full 3D region is too dense.
Provide a fallback message when there are too many rows or dimensions for a responsive render.

title: 10. Prediction Explorer and explanation
items: Prediction Explorer should be a primary feature, not just a small card. It demonstrates the model's logic to a user.
Capability
Behavior
Choose sample
Select a row from the dataset or enter feature values manually.
Validate input
Require all model-required features after preprocessing; validate ranges/types where possible.
Predict
Return predicted class or numeric value, plus probabilities when the estimator supports them.
Trace path
Show each condition evaluated in order, the observed feature value, whether the condition passed, and next node.
Highlight tree
Highlight every node and edge on the path in the tree canvas.
Leaf explanation
Show final leaf ID, training samples reaching leaf, class distribution/value, and prediction.
Compare examples
Advanced: compare two rows and show where their paths diverge.
Export explanation
Copy or download a readable explanation for the selected prediction.

EXPLANATION TEMPLATEIF feature_A ≤ threshold_1 → follow left branch; ELSE → follow right branch. Continue evaluating the conditions until a leaf is reached. THEN return that leaf's predicted class/value. Generate this text from the actual path, not from a separately hardcoded rule.

title: 11. Metrics and evaluation
items: 11.1 Classification
Accuracy: fraction of correctly classified examples.
Precision, recall, and F1-score per class, with macro and weighted averages.
Confusion matrix with true labels on one axis and predicted labels on the other; state axis convention.
Train and test scores shown separately to help detect overfitting.
Support count for each class.
Optional ROC-AUC / PR-AUC only when the score outputs and class setup make the metric valid.
11.2 Regression
MAE (mean absolute error).
MSE and RMSE where appropriate.
R² score, including a note that it can be negative on held-out data.
Actual-vs-predicted scatter with a y=x reference line.
Residual plot and residual summary.
Train and test scores shown separately.
11.3 Metrics card recommendation

Use five headline cards. The fifth card should be task-aware: feature count for a general summary, or rule count for classification explainability. Avoid showing classification-only values for regression.
Card
Classification
Regression
Accuracy or primary selected score
R² or primary selected score
Tree depth
Tree depth
Total nodes
Total nodes
Leaf nodes
Leaf nodes
Feature count or leaf/rule count
Feature count or leaf/rule count

title: 12. Feature importance and rules
items: 12.1 Feature analysis
Impurity-based feature importance from the fitted tree, clearly labeled as such.
Split frequency: number of internal nodes that use each feature.
Class or target distribution to help users understand imbalance.
Optional permutation importance on held-out data, with repeats and variability if available.
Tooltips defining the method and warning that impurity-based importance can favor some feature types or correlated predictors.
12.2 Rules and insights
Generate one rule for each reachable leaf: the conjunction of split conditions from root to leaf.
For classification, show predicted class and class distribution/probability where supported.
For regression, show predicted numeric value and appropriate target summary.
Show rule coverage/support and the number of training samples that reach the leaf.
Allow search/filter by predicted class, feature, threshold, and support.
Copy a rule and export the rule set as CSV or JSON.
Label rules as model logic, not causal explanations.

title: 13. UI/UX design system
items: Element
Recommendation
Brand palette
Charcoal #202722, warm white #FFFFFF, soft neutral #F3F5F3, emerald #21845B, muted purple #7963A8, amber #B7791F, coral #C45C50. Avoid blue as the dominant accent.
Color semantics
Use consistent class colors across tree, boundaries, tooltips, and legends. Never use color as the only indicator.
Typography
Readable sans-serif; 14–16 px body copy for desktop UI; technical labels must remain legible when zoomed.
Cards
Subtle borders, restrained shadow, consistent padding, no unnecessary nested cards.
Tree nodes
Rounded rectangles with compact labels; distinguish internal nodes and leaves using both label/shape and color.
Spacing
Use an 8 px spacing scale; keep primary tree canvas large and uncluttered.
Responsive behavior
Desktop: canvas and side panel side by side. Tablet: collapsible side panel. Mobile: stack canvas and details, with accessible horizontal canvas navigation.
Empty/loading/error states
Explain what is happening and how to recover; never show blank charts or raw stack traces to end users.
Accessibility
Keyboard operation, visible focus, semantic controls, high contrast, text alternatives, reduced motion, and non-color cues.

title: 15. Suggested API contracts
items: Keep payloads explicit and versionable. Do not send the entire raw dataset repeatedly if the backend can return a dataset ID and bounded previews.
Endpoint (example)
Purpose
Important request/response fields
POST /api/datasets
Upload and inspect dataset.
Request: file. Response: dataset_id, rows, columns, inferred_types, missing_summary, preview.
GET /api/datasets/{id}/preview
Retrieve bounded preview.
page/limit; rows and column metadata.
POST /api/models/decision-tree/train
Train tree and evaluate.
dataset_id, target, task, selected_features, parameters, test_size, random_state. Response: run_id, metrics, tree_summary.
GET /api/runs/{run_id}/tree
Return tree graph metadata.
nodes, edges, feature names, class names, task, run metadata.
GET /api/runs/{run_id}/nodes/{node_id}
Retrieve node details.
node_id, depth, split, threshold, impurity, samples, values, children, coverage.
POST /api/runs/{run_id}/predict
Predict one row or bounded batch.
features/rows. Response: prediction, probabilities if supported, leaf_id, path steps.
GET /api/runs/{run_id}/metrics
Get task-appropriate evaluation.
train/test metrics, confusion matrix or regression summaries, report.
GET /api/runs/{run_id}/importance
Feature importance.
method, feature names, scores.
POST /api/runs/{run_id}/export
Create export.
format and selected artifact; response includes a controlled download reference.
15.1 Example tree-node response shape
{  "node_id": 0,  "depth": 0,  "kind": "split",  "feature": "petal_length",  "threshold": 2.45,  "impurity": 0.66,  "samples": 120,  "value": [40, 40, 40],  "left_child": 1,  "right_child": 2}

This is an illustrative schema only; example values are not a promised result. Actual fields and numbers must come from the fitted estimator. Decide whether counts refer to the training subset or weighted samples and label them consistently.

title: 16. Data correctness and model behavior rules
items: Fit preprocessing only on training data; apply the fitted pipeline to test data and prediction inputs to prevent leakage.
Persist the exact feature order and preprocessing configuration used during training.
The tree, node details, path trace, feature importance, and metrics must all reference the same run_id.
Never show test metrics calculated on training rows as if they were held-out results.
If a model cannot produce class probabilities, do not invent a confidence percentage.
Use the correct impurity and metric definitions for the selected task and criterion.
For 2D/3D plots, state how unplotted features are handled; model output can depend on all input features.
Show warnings for tiny datasets, missing target values, single-class splits, high tree depth, and suspicious train/test score gaps.
Version and store model parameters, feature names, dataset fingerprint/ID, split seed, and metric definitions with each run.
Do not expose local filesystem paths, environment variables, database credentials, or stack traces to users.

title: 17. Step-by-step implementation roadmap
items: Recommended order: finish the data/model contract first, then make the tree correct, then add synchronized explanations, then add more chart types.
Phase 0 — Repository audit and design foundation
Inspect existing frontend, backend, routing, API patterns, styling, and test setup.
Confirm whether the project already uses React/Vite, FastAPI, scikit-learn, a database, and an authentication layer.
Create the Decision Tree page skeleton and shared palette, typography, spacing, and component conventions.
Agree on task types, dataset-size limits, API contracts, and run metadata.
Phase 1 — Dataset intake
Implement CSV upload, dataset ID, preview table, row/column counts, inferred types, missing-value summary.
Implement target selection and feature inclusion/exclusion.
Add explicit missing-value and categorical-encoding behavior.
Test malformed CSV, empty data, duplicate columns, missing target, mixed types, and large uploads.
Phase 2 — Train a real model
Implement classification/regression selection and parameter validation.
Create a reproducible train/test split and a fitted preprocessing pipeline.
Fit the correct scikit-learn estimator and return run_id plus metrics and tree summary.
Persist run metadata and verify that test metrics use held-out rows.
Phase 3 — Full tree canvas
Convert fitted tree arrays into a stable node/edge response.
Render root, internal nodes, leaves, connectors, labels, and branch conditions.
Add select node, zoom, pan, fit-to-screen, collapse/expand, layout orientation, and reset.
Build large-tree fallback behavior and an accessible tree outline.
Phase 4 — Node details and prediction path
Build the 12-field node details panel.
Add sample selection/manual feature input and prediction endpoint.
Return the actual path steps and final leaf ID.
Synchronize the path highlight in the tree with the explanation panel.
Test that manually computed paths match the estimator's decision_path/apply output.
Phase 5 — Core visual analytics
Add feature importance and target/class distribution.
Add 2D decision boundary with feature selectors, points, regions, tooltips, and legend.
Add classification confusion matrix/report OR regression actual-vs-predicted and residual plots.
Add train/test metric distinction and explain each metric.
Phase 6 — Rules and exports
Generate one IF–THEN rule per leaf from ancestor conditions.
Add search/filter/copy rules and CSV/JSON export.
Export tree as SVG/PNG and metrics as CSV.
Verify exported content matches the visible model run.
Phase 7 — Advanced visualization and pruning
Add 3D feature selection, point inspection, rotate/zoom/reset.
Add sampled decision-region rendering only when computation and performance are acceptable.
Add pruning/depth comparison and optionally permutation importance.
Label computational limitations and fall back gracefully.
Phase 8 — Hardening and release
Complete keyboard accessibility, focus, contrast, mobile layout, loading, empty, and error states.
Run frontend/backend/model correctness tests and performance checks.
Add telemetry only if appropriate and disclose it; avoid logging raw sensitive datasets unnecessarily.
Write user documentation and a sample walkthrough.

title: 18. Acceptance criteria by major feature
items: Feature
Done when…
Dataset intake
A user can upload a valid CSV, preview rows, select a target, and receive actionable errors for invalid input.
Training
The backend trains the requested task, returns a run ID, and reports metrics on the declared split.
Tree canvas
All reachable nodes and branches can be explored; node IDs and conditions match the estimator.
Node details
Clicking a node shows correct split, impurity, sample/value data, and children/leaf output.
Prediction path
A row prediction highlights the exact path and final leaf; the displayed route matches estimator traversal.
2D boundary
Feature selectors update the plot, legend is clear, and the view discloses treatment of other features.
3D view
Axis selectors, camera controls, point inspection, and reset work; unsupported/slow cases have fallback states.
Metrics
Classification and regression show appropriate metrics only, with train/test split clearly labeled.
Rules
Rules are generated from actual root-to-leaf conditions and can be exported.
Responsive/accessibility
Primary flows remain usable on narrow screens and with keyboard navigation.
Security
Upload limits, input validation, controlled exports, and safe error handling are in place.

title: 19. Testing checklist
items: Model correctness
☐ Node counts, child indices, thresholds, impurity and values match the fitted estimator.
☐ Leaf predictions match estimator.predict for tested rows.
☐ Path traversal matches decision_path/apply behavior.
☐ Feature importance values and labels match the selected method.
☐ Metrics match an independently computed test-set result.
Data handling
☐ Empty file, malformed CSV, duplicate headers, missing target, missing values, categorical values.
☐ Tiny dataset, one class, rare classes, constant features, high-cardinality categories.
☐ Feature order remains identical between training and prediction.
☐ Train/test split is reproducible with the same seed.
UI behavior
☐ Node selection persists and updates the side panel.
☐ Zoom, pan, fit, collapse/expand, orientation, and reset work.
☐ 2D selectors and 3D selectors update the appropriate plot.
☐ Loading, empty, success, validation error, and server error states are understandable.
☐ Exports open correctly and contain the currently selected run's information.
Performance and accessibility
☐ A representative medium tree remains responsive.
☐ Large trees can collapse or navigate without freezing the page.
☐ Keyboard focus is visible and controls have labels.
☐ Meaning is not conveyed by color alone.
☐ Reduced-motion and narrow-screen layouts remain usable.

title: 20. MVP versus later releases
items: Release
Include
Do not delay MVP for
MVP
CSV upload/preview, target selection, model training, five KPI cards, full tree canvas, node details, prediction path, rules, feature importance, task-appropriate metrics, 2D boundary, basic exports.
Highly polished 3D decision surfaces, counterfactual generation, complex saved-workspace management.
Release 1.1
Tree search, advanced node labels, pruning controls, permutation importance, improved large-tree navigation, PDF report.
Exotic chart types with limited learning value.
Release 2
3D decision regions, pairwise exploration, counterfactual or what-if analysis, model/run comparison, batch prediction, advanced diagnostics.
Features that are not backed by reliable model computations.

title: 21. Final recommended counts
items: PRACTICAL BUILD TARGETPlan for 8 navigation sections, 5 headline metric cards, 10 core visualization types, 12 node-detail fields, 10 tree-canvas interactions, 12 model-training controls, and 8 prediction-explorer capabilities. This is a complete product scope; release it in phases instead of building everything at once.

These counts are a product recommendation, not a technical limit. Some controls may be grouped or moved into Advanced Settings. Keep the initial interface simple, while ensuring the underlying architecture can grow.

title: 22. Recommended first sprint
items: Create the Decision Tree route and page shell with the neutral/emerald visual system.
Define typed interfaces for DatasetSummary, TrainingConfig, ModelRun, TreeNode, PredictionResult, and EvaluationMetrics.
Implement CSV preview and target selection.
Implement training endpoint for one supported classification dataset and one regression dataset.
Render a real fitted tree with node IDs and conditions.
Add node selection and node details.
Add one-row prediction with path trace and automated correctness tests.

After the first sprint, you should be able to train a real tree, click a node, inspect its actual statistics, and trace a prediction from root to leaf. That is the foundation on which all remaining visualizations should be built.

Appendix B — Glossary
Term
Plain-language meaning
Root node
The first decision in the tree.
Internal node
A node that applies a feature condition and splits rows into children.
Leaf node
A terminal node that returns a class or numeric prediction.
Threshold
The value used to decide which branch a sample follows.
Impurity
A measure of how mixed the target outcomes are at a node.
Depth
Number of edges from the root to a node; tree depth is the maximum level.
Samples
Number of training rows reaching a node; clarify whether weighted.
Decision boundary
The regions of feature space assigned different predictions.
Feature importance
A method-specific estimate of how much features contribute to the model.
Pruning
Reducing tree complexity to improve generalization or interpretability.
Data leakage
Using information during training that would not legitimately be available at prediction time.
